messages.subject: Online learning with INLA
parts:
Hi everyone,

Are there good examples of INLA being used for online learning with time series or spatiotemporal data. For example, if an AR(1) model is fit for time points 1:t, and then we want to generate a new fit for t+1, is it possible to do this using only the new data combined with the priors and latent state from the original model fit to t+1? (we have a computationally heavy spatiotemporal forecasting analysis, which would benefit from being able to use a smaller matrix for ongoing predictions)

Thanks!
Dan

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Online learning with INLA
parts:
The issue about online learning is that the Markov properties of the
latent is lost with marginalisation. the marginal for the latent state
at time t, conditioned on all previous time points, is no longer Markov
ie its precision matrix is dense, hence all computational benefits are
lost and you're back to dense matrix formulation and not within the INLA
(computational) framework.

so in a 'online'/dynamic framework where you want to do all the time one
step ahead forecast, and constantly revising the model with new data,
with INLA, then you use a moving window approach.

do t+1 forecast fitting the model from time 1 to t

observe new data y_t+1

do t+2 forecost fitting the model from time 2 to t+1, thus including
y_t+1 but removing y_1

you can use the first fit as an initial value for the second one hence
speeding it up.

this will implcitely gives you a 'model' with time-varying parameters
and hyperparameters, I guess you get my point. the length of the window
is whatever you're confortable with.

there is a way to let the posterior of the hyperparameters be the joint
prior in another inla() call, but that will not work here as there are
overlap of data in the two fits. unless you're willing to assuming some
discounting scheme, which is actually very reasonable here I would guess

Best
H
